newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan governors demand share of mineral wealth.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan governors demand share of mineral wealth.

text.p: Governors from Venezuela's 22 states marched to Congress on Wednesday to demand a share of the vast wealth produced by the oil and mining industries in their regions.
Accompanied by dozens of mayors, they handed over a petition with 1.2 million signatures in support of a bill that would break the central government's monopoly over mineral revenues.
Venezuela is the largest oil exporter in the western hemisphere and has plans to become one of the top ten gold producers in the world by early next century.
Edgar Valle Valle, president of the congressional committee that will study the bill, noted that Venezuela had received about $256 billion in oil revenues in the last three decades.

But while many of Venezuela's regions remain poor and underdeveloped, the modern capital Caracas is ringed by poor settlements populated by migrants from the interior of the country seeking work, he added.

Under the new bill, 10 percent of the government's tax revenues from oil and mining activities would be shared out between the 22 states, with nearly three quarters going to states in which oil and mining occur.

The money would be in addition to that regularly assigned to each state under the federal budget and would be spent on environmental protection, health and education programmes and scientific investigation.
Congressional President Cristobal Fernandez said Congress was in favour of the bill but warned that opposition would doubtless arise to it "because centralization will fight the death-blow."
